title: Hofrat Jähring to Georg Karl of Hesse-Darmstadt, 1792 (catalogue 2030): Porta table with the keyword "constantinopolitanus" written over the cipher by a second hand; the runs of the letter of 1 June 1792 deciphered, the upper runs of the report "Unterthänigster Bericht" read in part, its long cipher block decoded in fragments only

documents.shelfmark: HStAD D 4 Nr. 487/4, image 120, right page, foot (run 120.5) and image 121, left page (cipher block)
documents.route: Hofrat Jähring -> Georg Karl of Hesse-Darmstadt

plaintext.source: A second hand wrote the keyword over every cipher letter and "chandeltsnt" under run 120.5; no other decipherment.

transcription.notes: One pass only, four line fragments; the lines are overwritten by the key letters and strokes of the second hand. Not reconciled.

system.summary: Porta table with a running keyword, constantinopolitanus. The key letter picks one of 13 reciprocal alphabets (pairs ab, cd, ..., yz). The keyword starts again with each cipher run and runs on across line breaks. Latin lower-case letters inside clear German written in Kurrent; word division not kept. The looped upright d-shape is f; a heavy dot opening two runs on image 119 is a blotted o.
system.notes: Table chosen by testing Porta, Vigenère, Beaufort and variant on the first 22 letters of run 120.5 at all 20 offsets; only Porta at offset 0 read ("ernicht"). Frozen, then applied to all other runs (held out).

prior_solution.where: No edition or decipherment found: two web searches (12 Nov 2026) returned only finding-aid entries for the Jähring letter series; the vetting of 3 Nov 2026 found nothing in DECODE, Tomokiyo or Lasry. The only decipherment work on the leaves is the contemporary keyword alignment by a second hand on images 120-121.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2030) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, chose and froze the table, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (decryption, held-out test, mark check, reading counts)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: Images 119-122 of HStAD D 4 487/4 fetched at full size from digitalisate-he.arcinsys.de, one at a time, 2 s apart.

Keyword "constantinopolitanus" taken from the second hand's writing over the cipher of images 120-121. Porta, Vigenère, Beaufort and variant tested on the first 22 letters of run 120.5; Porta at offset 0 read. Key frozen (key_frozen.tsv).
Sign conventions written first; runs of images 119 and 120 (upper) in two passes from fresh crops; run 120.5 and four lines of 121 in one rough pass.

All 16 runs of 119 and 120 (upper) held out. Frozen key as frozen: 303/346 letters (0.876) match the final reading; with the two sign values set after the freeze (looped d = f, dot = o): 330/348 (0.948). Vigenère and Beaufort with the same keyword: at most 4/346 (0.012). Figures after the five letter corrections of the blind review; before them 298/346 (0.861) and 325/348 (0.934).

Runs decrypted mechanically and read as German with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes. Dan's reading checker on the German sentences: 0.70 (image 119) and 0.857 (image 120, upper runs); whole files 0.541 and 0.500 with the English notes counted.
Two web searches on Jähring, Georg Karl, Darmstadt, 1792 and cipher: finding-aid entries only.

Blind review by one independent AI language-model agent: about 230 cipher letters in 7 of the 16 runs and 14 letters of 121 copied from its own crops before seeing ours, about 93% letter agreement; five letters (q read as g or y) taken over, removing five marked changes; check_marks.py, the decryption and the held-out figures reproduced; the four sentences of image 120 read against the translation, 4 of 4 hold.

Integration check (13 Nov 2026): check_marks.py re-run (16 of 16 runs, all marks accounted for); own Porta decoder (keyword constantinopolitanus, restart per run, signs d-loop = f and dot = o) written from runs.json reproduces the mechanical decryption of all 16 runs; arcinsys image 120 fetched (plain GET) and runs 120.1-120.4 (about 160 letters) compared with the transcription: agree except one q/g-shape place at the end of 120.3. Held-out figures not re-run in full (scripts read; reading made with the key in view; two sign values set after the freeze). Status in progress: five gaps are not-attempted, no page.

Independent check (14 Nov 2026, Brice Dudout with Claude): a Porta decoder written from the statements of key.tsv alone reproduces decryption_119.txt and decryption_120.txt, 372 of 372 letters. At each marked change in the 119 runs the cipher letter that would give the wanted plaintext was computed and the place read on the arcinsys image 119: at 119.1 letter 10, 119.8 letter 9 and 119.12 letter 9 the image has v, not r, which gives 'cassengeschafte', 'gestimt' and 'miscredit' with no change. 119.2 letter 11 (v or w) and 119.6 letter 5 (s or f) stay open; 119.10 letter 8 is a clear q and 120.2 letter 10 a clear l (writer's slips). 119 now 19 words verbatim, 6 changed, 3 holes; check_marks.py passes.

outcome.method_basis: Keyword written by a contemporary second hand over the cipher of images 120-121; table (Porta) identified on 22 letters of run 120.5, frozen and tested on the 16 other runs.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Images 119-121 of a 226-image volume; the rest of the volume was not paged through for cipher, so the share is a rough estimate. Within images 119-121, under half of the cipher letters are in read runs; the block of 121 is not transcribed.

gaps.item: Run 120.5 (about 4 lines) and the cipher block of image 121 (about 10 lines)
gaps.detail: Overwritten by the second hand's key letters and strokes; only four line fragments transcribed, in one pass. The key works on all four and the key letters give each line's offset, so a careful transcription should read them.

gaps.item: Holes: 119L.2 (6 letters), the middle of 119.7 (6), the end of 119.13 (3), nine letters of 120.2
gaps.detail: The decryption does not read there; the transcription of these letters should be checked against the image.

gaps.item: 120.1, line 2, fourth letter (s or the looped d-shape)
gaps.detail: Undecided on this image; s gives the a of "anstatt", the looped d-shape would give x. Kept as s.
Not paged through for further cipher; short runs elsewhere were seen only on contact sheets.

texts.label: Image 119, letter of 1 June 1792: 12 short cipher runs
texts.summary: Business letter of 1 June 1792: the building goes slowly, the cash box, constant withdrawals of credit, people try to harm "our credit" but "we keep it all the same"; the correspondents "are well disposed"; Jacobi and a thousand guilders.
texts.note: Not prose: 12 runs of one to five words (28 words) inside a letter in clear German; each completes a clear sentence. Words: 19 verbatim from the signs, 6 with a marked change (14 Nov 2026: three r read as v on the image), 3 holes (119L.2, part of 119.7, end of 119.13). Clean share of the German sentences 0.70 (10 sentences); whole file 0.541. The clear frame is an approximate working transcription.

texts.label: Image 120 right, report "Unterthänigster Bericht": the four upper runs
texts.summary: The fair ended "gloriously" instead of getting stuck, as Jähring had feared; "he" made them a cash fund of 7,000 guilders at the fair; the prince is asked to say gracious things to him when he sees him.
texts.note: Four clause-length runs (37 words): 29 verbatim from the signs, 7 with a marked change, 1 hole (nine letters of 120.2). Clean share of the German sentences 0.857 (7 sentences); whole file 0.500. The clear frame is an approximate working transcription.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against translation_120.md: 4 of 4 sentences hold, the second with one 9-letter hole, and the translation matches with the holes kept. 37 cipher words checked; the agent's own copy of the four runs from the image gave five letter corrections, none of which changes a word.

texts.label: Run 120.5 and image 121: the rest of the report
texts.summary: Fragments only: "er nicht", "[...] aber er [hat] alles auf die verbindlichste Art gethan", "Kuppel ist gut", "vortheilhafte".
texts.note: About 14 cipher lines, overwritten by the second hand's key letters; only four line fragments transcribed in one pass. The words of the fragment reading cover 52 of the 98 transcribed letters (7/35, 20/25, 12/17, 13/21, changed letters included); the lines are not yet read. Whole-file clean share 0.286.
